Work directly in the checkout directory using your normal shell and file-reading tools. Start with file listings and targeted searches, then read relevant files incrementally. Inspect the supplied codebase and identify its core component: the connected set of responsibilities around which the application's main behavior and state are organized. Generate a single ASCII tree diagram showing that core component, its main parts, and their relationships. Choose the scope and level of detail that best explain the codebase. Ground the diagram in the source code.

Structure the tree as a decomposition of the core component:
  - Top-level branches are the core's main parts, not 3+1 categories. Each part appears in exactly one place.
  - Depth always means "is part of": a child is contained in, held by, or owned by its parent.
  - Place call, data-dependency and ownership lines under the part where they happen, with -> lines to the parts they reach. Do not give a flow its own top-level branch.
Cover breadth before depth:
  - Name every major subsystem of the core at depth 1-2, even in one line, before detailing any of them.
  - When a part has substantial structure of its own, give it a child line naming its sub-parts, even if you do not expand them.
  - Do not detail one part down to field layouts, allocators or buffers while another major part remains a single line.

Here is the "3+1" model of conceptual codebase models:
1. [REPLACED] Containment	      where code lives
2. [REPLACED] Lexical scope	    which names code can see
  -> *collapse* into 1. Modular structure
    I want to collapse Containment / Lexical scope into a single category, called modular structure, which:
    - abstracts out the source file level organization
      - but retains boundaries and visibility: what a component exposes versus keeps internal
    - retains dependency graph
    - groups components into higher level, logic-semantical categorizations
3. Call (dynamic)     which activation invoked which
4. Ownership          responsibility for state, storage, resources, and their lifetimes: who creates, retains, changes, or releases them
1. [SPECIAL] Data dependency   is a different kind of thing. It isn’t a fifth organizational choice; it is the record of what actually needs what for the program to compute its result. It’s a graph, and it exists before you decide how to organize anything.

Keep the following in mind when generating your diagram:
  - there should be 60/40 between code refs and nat lang

Few-shot examples (synthetic style references, not source facts):
Example 1: Incremental compiler
Incremental compiler -- reuse follows the module dependency graph
|
|-- [M] BuildGraph connects source modules to their compilation artifacts
|   |-- modules[moduleId]: ModuleUnit
|   |   |-- sourceHash -> immutable source bytes
|   |   |-- imports[] -> resolved module identities
|   |   `-- interfaceHash -> names and types visible to consumers
|   `-- units[unitId]: AnalysisUnit
|       |-- mutually dependent modules share one unit
|       `-- dependencies[] -> units whose interfaces must be available first
|
|-- [C] compileUnit(unitId) resolves one reusable result
|   |-- [D] member source hashes + dependency interfaces + compiler options
|   |   `-- analysisKey, including the compiler implementation version
|   |-- ArtifactCache.lookup(analysisKey)
|   |   |-- Hit -> recover typed modules and diagnostics
|   |   `-- Miss -> analyze the unit
|   |       |-- [C] Parser.parse(source) -> syntax with source spans
|   |       |-- [C] Binder.bind(syntax, dependencyInterfaces)
|   |       |   `-- Scope
|   |       |       |-- declarations[name] -> local Symbol
|   |       |       |-- parent -> enclosing lexical scope
|   |       |       `-- exports -> symbols visible across the module boundary
|   |       `-- [C] TypeChecker.check(boundUnit) -> typed modules + diagnostics
|   `-- Successful analysis -> Emitter.emit(typedModules, target)
|       |-- [D] typed modules + target version + emission options -> objectKey
|       `-- ObjectArtifact
|           |-- object code / exported interface / source map
|           `-- [O] ArtifactCache retains complete immutable entries
|               `-- consumers borrow artifacts; eviction follows cache policy
|
|-- [C] rebuild(changedPaths) propagates only relevant changes
|   |-- Capture new source hashes and resolve changed imports
|   |   `-- [D] updated graph -> regroup cycles and order affected units
|   |-- Reanalyze affected units
|   |   |-- Exported interface changed -> invalidate dependent analysis keys
|   |   `-- Interface unchanged -> consumers can reuse their typed modules
|   `-- [D] reachable object hashes + runtime + linker options -> bundleKey
|       `-- Linker.link(objects) produces the executable bundle
|           `-- changed implementation can require linking without retyping consumers
|
`-- [O] BuildScheduler controls transient execution
    |-- ready queue -> units whose dependency results are available
    |   `-- independent units may run concurrently
    |-- running[unitId] -> task + worker lease
    |   |-- [C] invoke compileUnit(unitId)
    |   `-- task settlement returns the worker lease
    |-- cancel(buildId)
    |   `-- stop scheduling -> signal tasks -> await settlement -> release snapshot
    `-- BuildResult retains bundle references and source-located diagnostics
        `-- [D] diagnostic spans + captured sources -> stable reported locations

Example 2: Telemetry ingestion service
Telemetry ingestion service
|
|-- [M] IngestGateway accepts batches from device connections
|   |-- accept(connection, envelope): BatchReceipt
|   |   |-- [D] credentials + device registry -> authorized tenant/device
|   |   `-- [C] decode -> validate envelope -> PartitionRouter.route(batch)
|   |       |-- Partition key = tenantId + deviceId
|   |       `-- One device's batches reach the same ordered partition
|   |-- [O] Retains connection state until disconnect
|   |   |-- pending[batchId] -> receipt waiter
|   |   `-- socket close detaches waiters; accepted work can still finish
|   `-- Admission limit
|       |-- available capacity -> enqueue batch
|       `-- full partition queue -> return retryable rejection
|
|-- [O] PartitionWorker owns one partition's ingestion progress
|   |-- Retained state
|   |   |-- queue: BoundedQueue<AcceptedBatch>
|   |   |   `-- accepted batches wait here before processing
|   |   |-- checkpoint: PartitionCheckpoint
|   |   |   |-- partitionId / committedOffset
|   |   |   `-- lastSequence[deviceId] -> latest committed device sequence
|   |   `-- lease: PartitionLease
|   |       |-- ownerId / epoch / expiresAt
|   |       `-- [D] current epoch -> authority to commit new progress
|   |
|   |-- [C] run() drains the queue one batch at a time
|   |   `-- process(batch)
|   |       |-- Establish batch identity
|   |       |   |-- key = tenantId + deviceId + batchId
|   |       |   `-- [C] EventStore.lookupReceipt(key)
|   |       |       |-- Same payload hash -> return committed receipt
|   |       |       |-- Different payload hash -> reject identity conflict
|   |       |       `-- Missing receipt -> prepare a new commit
|   |       |
|   |       |-- Normalize measurements
|   |       |   `-- [C] SchemaRegistry.resolve(batch.schemaVersion)
|   |       |       |-- [M] Exposes versioned field and unit definitions
|   |       |       `-- [D] raw samples + exact schema -> Measurement[]
|   |       |           |-- identity: tenantId / deviceId / sequence
|   |       |           |-- observation: timestamp / metric / value / unit
|   |       |           `-- provenance: batchId / schemaVersion / payloadHash
|   |       |
|   |       |-- Check sequence continuity
|   |       |   |-- [D] firstSequence + checkpoint.lastSequence[deviceId]
|   |       |   |   `-- next expected sequence or a detected gap
|   |       |   |-- Contiguous -> stage measurements
|   |       |   `-- Gap or overlap -> reject without advancing checkpoint
|   |       |
|   |       `-- Commit and acknowledge
|   |           |-- [C] EventStore.commit(batch, checkpoint, lease.epoch)
|   |           |   |-- [D] measurements + batch identity + next checkpoint
|   |           |   |   `-- one durable transaction
|   |           |   `-- Stale lease epoch -> reject the former owner
|   |           `-- After confirmed commit
|   |               |-- Install returned checkpoint
|   |               `-- Resolve gateway waiters with BatchReceipt
|   |                   `-- receipt confirms storage, not downstream indexing
|   |
|   `-- Lease loss or shutdown
|       |-- [C] Stop admission and stop dequeuing new work
|       |-- In-flight commit may have an uncertain outcome
|       |   `-- retry resolves through its durable batch receipt
|       `-- [O] Release queue entries and detach remaining waiters
|           `-- next owner restores progress from EventStore
|
|-- [M] EventStore binds stored events to durable progress
|   |-- [M] Exposes commit / lookupReceipt / restoreCheckpoint / scan
|   |-- Internal transaction
|   |   |-- Verify current partition lease epoch
|   |   |-- Append measurements with partition offsets
|   |   |-- Insert receipt under the unique batch identity
|   |   `-- Advance PartitionCheckpoint in the same commit
|   |       `-- failure rolls back events, receipt and checkpoint together
|   |-- [O] Retains the durable event log and retry receipts
|   |   |-- worker restarts leave both intact
|   |   `-- receipt retention defines the supported retry horizon
|   `-- scan(partitionId, afterOffset): EventPage
|       `-- [D] committed log + cursor -> ordered events and next cursor
|
`-- [M] ProjectionHost maintains independently rebuildable read models
    |-- [O] consumers[name]: ProjectionConsumer
    |   |-- cursor[partitionId] -> last applied event offset
    |   |-- handler: ProjectionHandler
    |   `-- cancellation + poll subscription
    |
    |-- Registered consumers
    |   |-- LatestReading
    |   |   |-- [D] device/metric + sequence -> newest accepted value
    |   |   `-- older replayed events cannot replace a newer reading
    |   `-- HourlySummary
    |       |-- [D] metric + observation timestamp -> aggregation bucket
    |       `-- count / sum / minimum / maximum
    |           `-- late observations update their original time bucket
    |
    |-- [C] poll() -> EventStore.scan() -> handler.apply(page)
    |   `-- Projection transaction
    |       |-- Apply only offsets beyond the stored consumer cursor
    |       `-- Save changed rows and cursor atomically
    |           `-- crash before commit -> safely read the same page again
    |
    `-- rebuild(name, newVersion)
        |-- [O] Create separate projection tables and fresh cursors
        |-- [C] Replay retained events while the current version serves reads
        `-- [D] rebuilt cursors + captured log positions -> readiness
            `-- switch readers after catch-up; retire the previous tables

Example 1 places two operations (compileUnit, rebuild) at the top level; in your tree, nest operations under the part that owns them.
Use the examples as a varied pool of representational choices. Let the supplied evidence determine depth, branching, density, and relationship types; do not copy their domain facts, exact shapes, counts, or require every tag.

Tree validation: Start with one root title, followed by a connector-only line. Place all other content beneath explicit branches. Do not insert annotations, references, legends, or explanatory text between the root title and its first branch.

Root title
|
|-- First component
|   `-- Supporting detail
`-- Second component

Before returning, verify that every branch belongs to the single root.

Return a JSON object with exactly one field, "ascii", containing the diagram string. Return exactly one ASCII tree with one root, printable ASCII characters, spaces and LF newlines. No Markdown fences or surrounding prose. The complete tree must fit within 20000 characters. Do not add separate side diagrams.

{"ascii":"Pi coding-agent session core -- AgentSession coordinates behavior and state
|
|-- Runtime assembly and lifetime [packages/coding-agent/src/core/sdk.ts; agent-session-runtime.ts]
|   |-- createAgentSession(): constructs Agent, CacheWarmer and AgentSession
|   |   |-- Restores transcript, model, thinking level and initial tool selection
|   |   `-- -> SessionManager.buildSessionContext(), ModelRuntime, SettingsManager
|   |-- AgentSessionRuntime: holds current session and cwd-bound AgentSessionServices
|   |   |-- switchSession(), newSession(), fork/import support and host rebinding
|   |   |-- Replacement -> abort old session, emit session_shutdown, dispose, create next runtime
|   |   `-- Services retain ModelRuntime, SettingsManager and ResourceLoader references
|   `-- Application boundary [packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts; modes/]
|       |-- InteractiveMode, runPrintMode and runRpcMode supply different I/O layers
|       `-- -> AgentSession commands and subscriptions; runtime host handles replacement
|
|-- Session orchestration [packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session.ts:409]
|   |-- Public control: prompt(), steer(), followUp(), abort(), waitForIdle(), subscribe()
|   |   |-- Private state: active/preflight flags, displayed queues, pending custom messages
|   |   `-- Holds -> Agent, SessionManager, settings, resources, model runtime and extension runner
|   |-- Input preparation: _preparePrompt(), _prepareRun(), _startRun()
|   |   |-- -> ExtensionRunner for commands, input interception and before_agent_start
|   |   |-- Skills + prompt templates + normalized images + system/tool changes -> starting messages
|   |   `-- -> Agent.prompt(); retries or boundary continuation -> Agent.continue()
|   |-- Event bridge: _handleAgentEvent(), _emitAgentSettled()
|   |   |-- Agent events -> extension handlers first, then public subscribers
|   |   |-- Completed messages -> SessionManager.appendMessage()/appendCustomMessageEntry()
|   |   `-- agent_settled marks completion after recovery and extension continuations finish
|   `-- Cancellation and disposal
|       |-- Owns run coordination, listeners and cancellation for auxiliary work
|       `-- dispose() -> abort work, invalidate extension contexts, unsubscribe, cancel cache warming
|
|-- Turn engine: Agent [packages/agent/src/agent.ts:193; agent-loop.ts:172]
|   |-- Live state and scheduling
|   |   |-- Transcript, selected model, thinking level, executable tools and streaming status
|   |   `-- Steering/follow-up queues, active-run promise, AbortController and event listeners
|   |-- runAgentLoop()/runAgentLoopContinue(): provider-independent turn execution
|   |   |-- Inner loop handles assistant responses, tool results and steering input
|   |   |-- Outer loop accepts follow-ups after the agent would otherwise stop
|   |   `-- prepareRequest/prepareNextTurn/finishTurn -> AgentSession-installed hooks
|   |-- streamAssistantResponse()
|   |   |-- Context transforms + convertToLlm() -> normalized provider messages
|   |   `-- Injected streamFunction -> ModelRuntime.streamSimple(); deltas -> lifecycle events
|   `-- executeToolCalls()/runToolCall()
|       |-- Argument preparation, before/after hooks, sequential or parallel dispatch
|       |-- -> callable tool implementations; results return to the conversation
|       `-- Truncated assistant tool arguments produce failed results instead of executing
|
|-- Canonical history: SessionManager [packages/coding-agent/src/core/session-manager.ts:995]
|   |-- Append-only session tree, persisted as JSONL or held in memory
|   |   |-- Header, entries, parent links, current leaf, entry index and labels
|   |   `-- Entry kinds include messages, model/thinking changes, summaries, edits and custom data
|   |-- append*(), getBranch(), getTree(), branch(), createBranchedSession()
|   |   |-- Appending creates a child at the current leaf
|   |   `-- Branching moves the leaf without deleting alternate history
|   |-- buildSessionProjection()/buildSessionContext() [session-manager.ts:544]
|   |   |-- Selected branch + latest compaction + context edits -> effective messages and settings
|   |   `-- -> Agent live context; raw stored history and model-visible history remain distinct
|   `-- Session inspection and export [agent-session.ts; session-export.ts; export-html/]
|       |-- Session statistics, usage totals, JSONL export and HTML rendering
|       `-- Depend on -> stored entries, current projection and tool renderers
|
|-- Context maintenance and recovery [packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session.ts]
|   |-- Compaction: compact(), _checkCompaction(), _runAutoCompaction()
|   |   |-- Helpers: prepareCompaction(), token estimates and compact() [core/compaction/]
|   |   |-- Branch projection + model limits + settings -> retained context and summary request
|   |   |-- -> ExtensionRunner may cancel or supply a summary; otherwise -> model stream
|   |   `-- Summary -> SessionManager.appendCompaction(); refreshed projection -> Agent
|   |-- Tree navigation: navigateTree() and generateBranchSummary()
|   |   |-- Leaving/target branches + summary policy -> optional branch summary
|   |   `-- -> SessionManager branch operations and restored Agent context
|   `-- Retry policy: _handlePostAgentRun(), _prepareRetry()
|       |-- Retry budget/backoff, failed response and abortable wait are session-owned
|       |-- Failed attempts stay in raw history but are omitted from the model projection
|       `-- Transient failure -> Agent.continue(); context overflow -> compaction recovery
|
|-- Tool environment and shell execution [packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session.ts; tools/]
|   |-- Definition-first registry and loadout
|   |   |-- Built-in/custom/extension definitions, executable registry and pending tool names
|   |   |-- Allow/deny matching, active/callable exposure and hidden declarations
|   |   `-- setActiveToolsByName() and prompt preparation -> Agent tools and transcript declarations
|   |-- Built-in tools [core/tools/index.ts]
|   |   |-- Default coding set: read, bash, edit, write
|   |   |-- Additional tools: grep, find, ls, powershell
|   |   `-- Supporting parts: operation adapters, file-mutation queue, truncation and renderers
|   |-- NestedToolCallRunner [core/nested-tool-calls.ts]
|   |   |-- ctx.executeTool() -> registered tools through the normal tool-call hooks
|   |   `-- Nested calls and usage -> parent tool-result message
|   `-- executeBash()/recordBashResult() [agent-session.ts:4003; core/bash-executor.ts]
|       |-- Owns shell cancellation and pending BashExecutionMessage results
|       |-- -> executeBashWithOperations(); streamed output -> session subscribers
|       `-- Results -> history/context; insertion waits when necessary to preserve tool-result order
|
|-- Extension and resource subsystem [packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/; resource-loader.ts]
|   |-- DefaultResourceLoader: discovers, loads and retains project/global resources
|   |   |-- Extensions, skills, prompt templates, themes, context files and system-prompt text
|   |   |-- Package/resource resolution, source metadata and load diagnostics
|   |   `-- Resources -> AgentSession prompt construction and runtime rebuilding
|   |-- ExtensionRunner [core/extensions/runner.ts:364]
|   |   |-- Retains loaded extensions, runtime registrations, mode/UI bindings and error listeners
|   |   |-- Exposes command/context APIs, event hooks, tools and provider registration
|   |   |-- Bound actions -> AgentSession; session reads -> SessionManager; model access -> ModelRegistry
|   |   `-- Input/context/tool/provider/boundary hooks can influence execution, not just observe it
|   |-- Built-in extensions [packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/index.ts]
|   |   |-- llama.cpp, codemode, tool-search and MCP
|   |   `-- Codemode, tool-search and MCP registrations may be replaced by other extensions
|   `-- AgentSession.reload() [core/agent-session.ts:3815]
|       |-- Shutdown and invalidate old runner; preserve flags and intended tool selection
|       `-- -> reload settings/resources, rebuild registry/runner and emit session_start
|
|-- Model access and request caching [packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts]
|   |-- ModelRuntime: canonical model/auth facade implementing pi-ai Models
|   |   |-- Holds MutableModels, RuntimeCredentials, ModelConfig and availability snapshots
|   |   |-- Provider composition includes built-ins, configured/extension providers and virtual models
|   |   |-- getAvailable(), getAuth(), login/logout, registerProvider(), resolveModel(), streamSimple()
|   |   `-- Model + transcript + credentials/configuration -> resolved provider request
|   |-- Provider engine boundary
|   |   |-- -> @earendil-works/pi-ai for catalog, credential and streaming operations
|   |   `-- SDK request wrapper applies retry/timeout settings and extension provider hooks
|   |-- Session model selection [core/agent-session.ts:2644]
|   |   |-- setModel()/cycleModel()/setThinkingLevel() update live selection and clamp capabilities
|   |   `-- -> Agent state and SessionManager metadata; optional persistence -> SettingsManager
|   `-- CacheWarmer [core/cache-warmer.ts; core/sdk.ts:335]
|       |-- Tracks eligible session requests, warming status and context-validity checks
|       |-- -> ModelRuntime for warming; recorded warming entries -> session events/history
|       `-- Session settlement drives warming; disposal cancels it
|
`-- Configuration policy: SettingsManager [packages/coding-agent/src/core/settings-manager.ts:272]
    |-- Holds global/project settings, merged effective settings and project-trust state
    |   `-- Storage, dirty-field tracking, serialized writes and load/save diagnostics
    |-- Policies: model defaults, tools, queue modes, compaction, retries, transport and shell/image options
    |   `-- -> Session orchestration, tool construction, context recovery and model requests
    `-- create()/reload()/setters provide persistent policy without owning the conversation
        `-- Cwd-bound service creation -> correct project settings for each replacement session"}
